title: SCENT: an $83 open-hardware three-sensor electronic nose, with the data and analysis code for Nambi et al., Sensors
description:
Hardware design files, raw sensor logs, acquisition code and analysis code supporting:

Nambi, T.; Bhimireddy, N.; McElroy, J. P. Isolating the contributions of resistance-ratio normalization and humidity fusion in a minimal three-sensor electronic nose. Manuscript sensors-4609768, Sensors.

SCENT is a low-cost electronic nose built from three MQ-series metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors in a 3D-printed PETG chamber with active purge fluidics. Acquisition, feature extraction and classification all run on a Raspberry Pi 5 with no network dependency.

This deposit contains: the raw sensor logs for both acquisitions (450 primary trials and 245 ablation trials, 19 CSV files); the acquisition script; the analysis script for the single-seed results; four further scripts covering the ten-seed sweep, the leave-one-sensor-out ablation and its preparation-level repeat, the learning curve, and the CCS811 exclusion checks, each with its JSON output; the chamber STL and the Fritzing wiring sketch; and the itemized bill of materials behind the USD 83 figure. Nothing is withheld from the deposit.

Code is released under the MIT License; the data under CC BY 4.0, as recorded in LICENSE and LICENSE-DATA.
